t: 3530 – Maximum Profit from Valid Topological Order in DAG
o: Choose a topological order maximizing Σ score[i]·position(i). With n ≤ 22, bitmask DP over subsets is natural: dp[mask] = best profit having placed exactly the nodes in mask. Node i can be placed next iff all its prerequisites are in mask; its position is popcount(mask)+1. Example 2: order [0,2,1] gives 1·1+3·2+6·3=25.
k: Node i is available in state mask iff prereqMask[i] ⊆ mask.
Position of the next placed node = popcount(mask)+1.

a.i: Iterate masks in increasing order; for each reachable mask try appending every available node, transitioning dp[mask] + score[i]·(bits+1).
s: Build prereqMask[v] = OR of bits of all predecessors.
dp[0]=0; for each mask, for each unused i with prereqs satisfied, relax dp[mask|1<<i].
a.t: O(2ⁿ·n) — each of 2ⁿ states scans n candidate nodes; n ≤ 22 gives ~92M simple ops.

w: Bitmask DP is essentially forced by n ≤ 22. Micro-optimizations: prune unreachable masks, precompute popcounts. Profit fits in 64 bits (22·1e5·22). Follow-up: minimize profit, or weighted edges between consecutive placements.
